topics.title: Getting started
topics.summary: Create a book, or bring one over from GnuCash.
topics.keywords: start begin new book open gnucash import migrate first

blocks.value: A **book** is your whole set of accounts and transactions, kept in one file you own. FinvestLens never uploads it anywhere.
Start a book

items: Choose File ▸ New Book… (⌥⌘N) and pick where to keep the file.
Choose a starter chart of accounts, or start empty and add your own.
Add your bank and credit-card accounts, and enter their opening balances.

blocks.value: Coming from GnuCash

Choose File ▸ Import GnuCash… and pick your `.gnucash` file. Accounts, transactions, prices, scheduled transactions and business records all come across, and you can export back to GnuCash at any time.
Everything you do is undoable with ⌘Z — including imports. If a change looks wrong, undo it rather than repairing it by hand.

topics.title: Accounts
topics.summary: The chart of accounts, and how the sidebar is organised.
topics.keywords: account chart tree parent placeholder hidden favourite type asset liability equity income expense

blocks.value: Accounts form a tree. A parent account shows the total of everything beneath it, so you can group *Expenses:Car:Fuel* and *Expenses:Car:Insurance* under one *Car* heading and still see them separately.
Account types

rows: What you own — bank accounts, cash, investments, property.
What you owe — credit cards, loans, mortgages.
Money coming in — salary, dividends, interest.
Money going out — the categories you spend in.

blocks.value: Keeping the sidebar tidy

items: **Favourites** pin the accounts you use most to the top of the sidebar.
**Placeholder** accounts group children but take no transactions of their own.
**Hidden** accounts stay out of the sidebar until you switch them back on.
The filter box at the top of the sidebar narrows the tree as you type.

topics.title: Recording transactions
topics.summary: The register, splits, and editing a row in place.
topics.keywords: transaction register enter split memo transfer edit double entry balance style columns

blocks.value: Select an account in the sidebar to open its **register** — one row per transaction, with a running balance. The row at the bottom is where you type a new one.
Entering a transaction

items: Type the date, then the description — earlier entries autocomplete as you type.
Choose the other account (the category, or where the money went).
Enter the amount and press ⏎.

blocks.value: Every transaction moves money **between two accounts**, so it always balances. That is what makes the reports add up.
Splits

A transaction can touch more than two accounts — a pay slip split into salary, tax and superannuation, or a shopping trip split across categories. Select the row and press ⌘E, or click its disclosure arrow, to open it out — notes, tags and every leg, edited in the register itself.

How much each row shows is up to you: View ▸ Register Style switches between one line per transaction (Basic Ledger), detail on the selected row (Auto Details), and every row open (Transaction Journal). View ▸ Columns switches off the columns you do not use.

topics.title: Finding transactions
topics.summary: Search operators, saved searches, and jumping around.
topics.keywords: search find filter query operator saved tag amount date jump

blocks.value: The search box above the register searches the description, amount and date. It also understands operators, which can be combined:

rows: Postings to a matching account (`category:` also works).
On or after a date — or `today`, `-7d`, `-2w`, `-3m`, `-1y`.
Only transactions with a document attached.

blocks.value: Put `-` in front of any term to exclude it — `-tag:work` hides work spending.
Elsewhere

items: **Find…** (⌘F) searches across every account, not just the open one.
**Find Account…** (⌘I) jumps straight to an account by name.
Save a search you keep repeating, and it comes back in the search menu.

topics.title: Saving and keeping the book safe
topics.summary: Saving, autosave, locking, network drives, and the audit log.
topics.keywords: save autosave lock nas smb network shared backup audit undo repair

blocks.value: Saving
Your changes are held in a working copy and written back to the file when you press ⌘S, when autosave runs, or when you close the book. Autosave and its interval live in Settings ▸ General.
Sharing a book across machines

A book can live on a NAS or shared folder. FinvestLens takes a lock while it is open so a second machine cannot overwrite your work; if the app behind a lock has gone away, you can break the lock and open anyway.
Locking the screen
Security ▸ Lock Now (⇧⌘L) hides the book until you authenticate. Turn on *Require Authentication to Open* to be asked every time.
If something looks wrong

items: ⌘Z undoes anything, including an import.
**Book ▸ Repair Book** runs the same checks as GnuCash's Check & Repair, and changes nothing until you choose Clean Up.
An audit log is kept beside the book, recording each edit.

topics.title: Importing bank files
topics.summary: CSV, QIF, OFX, MT940 and CAMT.053 — and how matching works.
topics.keywords: import bank csv qif ofx qfx mt940 camt statement download duplicate match profile

blocks.value: Choose Book ▸ Import Bank File… (⌥⌘I) and pick what your bank gave you. The format is detected from the file itself — CSV, QIF, OFX/QFX, SWIFT MT940/MT942 and ISO 20022 CAMT.053 are all read.
The review screen
Nothing is written until you say so. Each row shows what FinvestLens intends to do, and you can change the account, the category or the date before importing.

items: Rows you have already imported are marked as duplicates and skipped.
A payment that matches the other side of a transfer already in the book is completed rather than duplicated.
Rows nothing could categorise still import — parked in Imbalance for the Uncategorised review to sweep up later.

blocks.value: CSV columns
For CSV, tell FinvestLens which column is the date, description and amount. Save that as a profile and the next file from the same bank is set up for you.

topics.title: Reading PDFs with Apple Intelligence
topics.summary: Turn statements, invoices and dividend notices into transactions.
topics.keywords: pdf smart import apple intelligence ocr scan statement invoice dividend attachment

blocks.value: Book ▸ Smart Import PDFs… (⇧⌘I) reads bank statements, dividend statements and invoices **on this device** and turns them into transactions for you to review. Nothing is sent anywhere.
What it does

items: Reads the rows out of the document, including scanned pages.
Matches each one to a transaction already in your book, in any account.
Links the PDF to that transaction, and suggests a category.

blocks.value: **Match Attachments…** (⇧⌘M) does the same for receipts you already have — PDFs or photos: pick the files, and each is paired with its transaction and filed.

Receipts from a trip match too. A card charged overseas posts in your own currency, so nothing on the receipt looks like the amount in your book — but the card issuer writes the original into the transaction, and that figure is matched exactly. No exchange rate, nothing to set up.

A file that matches nothing keeps its row and says why. **Manually Edit…** opens the transaction editor with the document's date, vendor and amount already filled in — for a cash purchase that was never on a statement, or one whose statement you have not imported yet.
Always read the review screen. On-device reading is good but not perfect — statements with unsigned debit and credit columns and no running balance are the case most worth checking.

topics.title: Categorising and rules
topics.summary: Auto-categorise from your own history, and write rules.
topics.keywords: categorise categorize rule auto uncategorised imbalance payee learn bulk

blocks.value: Auto-categorise

FinvestLens learns from work you have already done: when a payee has been categorised before, it proposes the same treatment — including the split breakdown for things like salary or dividends. Where a payee is genuinely ambiguous it abstains rather than guessing.
Rules

A rule matches on the description, amount, account or tag and then sets a category, renames the transaction, adds tags, or links a payment to a bill. Rules run when you import, and you can apply them to history at any time.
Bulk editing
Select several transactions and use Bulk Edit to apply one change to all of them. Only the fields you switch on are changed; everything else is left alone.

topics.title: Reconciling an account
topics.summary: Agree your book with a bank statement, to the cent.
topics.keywords: reconcile reconciliation statement cleared balance tick difference

blocks.value: Reconciling proves your records match the bank's. Choose Book ▸ Reconcile Account… (⇧⌘R) with the account selected.

items: Enter the statement's closing balance and date.
Tick the transactions that appear on the statement — matching ones are ticked for you.
When the difference reaches zero, choose Finish.

blocks.value: Finished transactions are marked **reconciled** and are protected from casual edits. If you need to go back, Re-open Last Reconciliation… returns them to cleared so you can work through the statement again.

A difference that will not close is usually a missing transaction, a duplicate, or an amount typed with digits transposed. The running difference at the bottom tells you exactly how much you are looking for.

topics.title: Scheduled transactions and bills
topics.summary: Recurring entries, reminders, and what is coming up.
topics.keywords: scheduled recurring repeat bill reminder due loan mortgage formula

blocks.value: A scheduled transaction repeats on a pattern you choose — weekly, monthly, on a day of the month, or any interval. FinvestLens tells you when one is due and enters it when you confirm.

items: **Up Next** on the dashboard shows what is due and what is overdue.
Set a schedule to be created a few days early if you like to see it coming.
A schedule can use a **formula** — you are asked for the varying amount each time it falls due.

blocks.value: Loans
The Loan Calculator builds a repayment schedule and can create the scheduled payment for you, split into interest and principal.
Bills
A rule can mark a payment as settling a particular bill, so the reminder clears exactly rather than by guessing at the name.

topics.title: Budgets
topics.summary: Plan what you mean to spend, then see how it went.
topics.keywords: budget plan spending actual variance auto suggest

blocks.value: A budget sets a planned amount per account per period. Open it with Book ▸ Budget… (⌘B).

items: **Auto-budget** fills in amounts from what you actually spent.
**Suggest Budget** proposes monthly figures from six months of spending, using Apple Intelligence on this device.
The dashboard's Cashflow vs Budget card shows how the current period is tracking.

blocks.value: Budget-versus-actual is a report like any other, so you can export it or keep it as a favourite.

topics.title: Receipts and documents
topics.summary: Attach files to transactions and keep the links working.
topics.keywords: attachment document receipt invoice link file folder relative path

blocks.value: Any transaction can have documents attached — a receipt, an invoice, a dividend statement. The Attachments panel beside the register shows the selected transaction's file; turn it on with **View ▸ Attachments** in the register toolbar.
Where files live

Set a document folder in Settings ▸ Documents. Files inside it are linked **relatively**, the same way GnuCash does it, so the book and its documents can move together — onto a NAS, or to a new Mac — without breaking.

items: **Link File…** points at a file where it already is.
**Add Web Link…** stores a URL instead of a file.
**Remove Link** unlinks only — your file is never deleted.

topics.title: Investments and prices
topics.summary: Holdings, price updates, cost basis and targets.
topics.keywords: investment security share stock price quote portfolio dividend capital gain cost basis ticker

blocks.value: A security account holds units — shares, units in a fund, or a currency. Buys, sells, dividends and returns of capital are recorded through the Stock Transaction sheet, which works out the cost basis and any gain for you.
Prices

items: **Update Prices** (⇧⌘U) fetches the latest quotes for everything you hold.
Yahoo and Stooq need no key; EODHD, Alpha Vantage, Finnhub and Twelve Data take a free API key, set in Settings ▸ Pricing.
Keys are kept in your keychain on this device — never in the book file.

blocks.value: Price targets
Set a target on a security and the dashboard tells you when the latest quote crosses it.
Dividends and franking
Record Dividend… books the cash and, where it applies, the franking credits — so the tax reports have what they need at the end of the year.

topics.title: Reports and statements
topics.summary: Statements, charts, decks and the end-of-year pack.
topics.keywords: report statement balance sheet income profit loss trial cash flow pdf export deck review

blocks.value: Reports ▸ Reports… (⌘R) opens the gallery: balance sheet, income statement, trial balance, cash flow, budget, tax, investment and business reports.

items: Change the period and options at the top of any report.
Save a report with its settings as a **favourite** to come back to it.
Export any report as a PDF, or share it.

blocks.value: Presentation decks

**Financial Review** presents a period as a slide deck — one message per slide, with charts and commentary written on this device from the figures on the slide. **Investment Review** does the same for the portfolio.
End of year
The **Financial Year Pack** gathers the statements you need at tax time into one PDF, in reading order.

topics.title: Planning ahead
topics.summary: Debts, a lifetime plan, tax estimates and a wellbeing score.
topics.keywords: plan planner debt avalanche snowball retirement lifetime tax estimate wellbeing forecast

blocks.value: Debt Reduction Planner

Enter what you can put toward debts each month and compare **avalanche** (highest rate first) with **snowball** (smallest balance first) — you see the payoff date and the interest saved against paying minimums.
Lifetime Planner
A long-range projection seeded from your own book, with assumptions you can edit and one-off life events you can add. Figures can be shown in today's money.
Tax estimator
An estimate built from the accounts you mark as income and deductions, using editable brackets that default to Australian resident rates.
Financial Wellbeing

A transparent score from four measures in your own books — savings rate, months of spending covered by cash, non-mortgage debt against income, and the recent spending trend. Every component is shown, with how it was worked out.
These are estimates from your own figures and assumptions. They are not financial or tax advice.

topics.title: Savings goals
topics.summary: Set money aside toward something, and track the push.
topics.keywords: goal saving target challenge set aside holiday emergency fund deposit

blocks.value: A goal earmarks part of an account toward something — a holiday, an emergency fund, a deposit. The money stays where it is; the goal just tracks how much of it is spoken for.

items: Add or withdraw against a goal as you save.
A goal can have a target amount and a target date, and shows what is left to go.
A **challenge** is a time-boxed push on one goal, if you like a deadline.

topics.title: Small business
topics.summary: Customers, suppliers, invoices, bills and billable time.
topics.keywords: business customer vendor supplier invoice bill payment aging receivable payable job employee tax invoice time mileage

blocks.value: Business ▸ Customers, Vendors & Invoices… (⇧⌘B) opens the business hub: customers, vendors, employees, jobs, invoices, bills and billing terms.
Invoicing

items: Create an invoice for a customer and add its line items.
Post it — that books the amount to accounts receivable.
When you are paid, use Process Payment to settle it.

blocks.value: Reports

items: **Receivable Aging** and **Payable Aging** show what is owed and how late it is.
An invoice can be printed as an Australian Tax Invoice.
A **credit note** reduces what is owed, rather than adding to it.

blocks.value: Time and mileage
Log billable hours or travel, then gather them onto a customer invoice.

topics.title: Emergency records
topics.summary: Key details kept with the book, behind authentication.
topics.keywords: emergency record insurance policy contact account number authentication touch id

blocks.value: Emergency Records keeps the details someone would need in a hurry — insurance policies, account numbers, contacts — alongside the book rather than scattered across notes and drawers.
The screen asks for Touch ID or your password each time it opens, and the records stay inside your book file.

topics.title: GnuCash, Ledger and the command line
topics.summary: Move your data in and out, and script reports.
topics.keywords: gnucash ledger export import cli finlens command line journal interchange

blocks.value: GnuCash
FinvestLens reads and writes GnuCash XML, so you can move a book either way without losing detail — accounts, splits, prices, schedules and business records all survive the trip.
Ledger journals
File ▸ Export Ledger Journal… (⇧⌘E) writes a plain-text Ledger journal, and File ▸ Import Ledger Journal… reads one back.
The finlens command line
`finlens` is a read-only command-line reporter over your book, modelled on Ledger's. It is safe to run while the app has the book open — it takes no lock and never writes.

rows: The book as a Ledger journal.
